en: That Givel... to have come this\nfar in such a short time...!

Mastima. Reports on the
damage in each sector are
coming in. I will share them with
you.
Right.
Tika, Ricardo.
Yes! I'll go arrange the rescue\nteams right away!
And big brother...
I just need to go check if any\nother pests have slipped in,\nright?
Yeah! Please do!
I'm counting on you both.
Yes! Rekoro, let's go!
Understood!

This is Tika Blanche. Please
deploy medical teams from
Grand Meteora! I will take
command on-site!
...Tika has really grown strong,\nhasn't she?

Yeah. To be honest, I'm not
sure if I could even hold my
own against her in a direct
fight now.
That just shows how strong\nher will was.
It seems she's even earned\nherself a certain social\nstanding here in Ex Giva...
She's a strong girl.
For Tika's sake, we've seriously\ngotta keep our heads in the\ngame from here on out!
Hey, you over there. Verda\nKleiman, and Valka S90.
Hm?
...What is it?
The three of you, come with\nme for a moment.
What on earth is this about?

<font color=blue>Mastima</font>: Now that you have
experienced this battle, I wish
to ask you once more: are you
truly prepared?
<font color=blue>Verda</font>: Prepared for what?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font>: Are you willing to\nsacrifice your own lives for the\nsake of complete strangers?
<font color=blue>Valka</font>: I don't understand the\nintent of your question, Master\nMastima.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font>: The battles ahead in
Daftine will be far more
dangerous than you can
possibly imagine.
<font color=blue>Verda</font>: And what of it?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font>: The three of you are\nnot natives of this star system.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font>: I am asking if you
have the resolve to throw
yourselves into a life-or-death
struggle for the future of a
system that is not your own.

<font color=blue>Verda</font>: Exactly, exactly. That's
why you modified our ship in
the first place, isn't it? Isn't it
a bit late to be asking now?

<font color=blue>Mastima</font>: When you first
arrived in this sector, you
failed to realize that an Ex Giva
existed on this moon.
However, on the other hand,\nwhile Givel knew that the Ex\nGiva was here,
They managed to slip through\nmy crest barrier and send that\nmonster after you.
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Do you understand\nwhat this means?
<font color=blue>Valka</font> I... I don't...
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> I don't know if Ex\nanticipated this, but...

The enemy you are about to
face is all the more dangerous
if they possess the common
sense of an advanced planet.
Especially those who try to\napply "common sense" to this\nuniverse.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Whether they are
users of Summoning Crest Arts
or servants of Daftes―you
have no idea what kind of
irreversible catastrophe such
trivial assumptions can lead to.

What you are about to
encounter is the very definition
of the "unknown," something
that cannot even be compared
to me.

Being protected by the
technology of an advanced
planet provides no guarantee
of safety.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> And what about you?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Me?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> How long do you think\nI have lived in this star\nsystem?
I'm afraid Tika and I simply\ndon't share the same level of\nattachment.

Especially you, Valka S90. Your
assigned mission is
investigation, not intervention
in local affairs.

If you were to fall here, there
would be no one to bring
information on Givel and
Daftine back to Ex.

That would be a significant
loss for the universe protected
by the power of Vandione and
Ex.
That is not an outcome I\ndesire.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> ...
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> If you are so\nconcerned about this\ncompanion of yours, Evelysse,
I can at least help you rescue\nher from Givel's grasp, so if\nyou just wait here...
Mastima. You're surprisingly\nkind, aren't you?

But I don't want you
misunderstanding one thing.
The Captain, Valka, and of
course myself,
I know full well that "common sense" never existed in this universe to begin with. That is the kind of journey we have made.
note: glossary-waive: ハナ (ハナから is the idiom 'from the start', not the name Hana); the engine dropped the subject ("know full well...")

en: Are you referring to the\nconclusion of that business\nwith the Burning Death?
If you already know, then this\nwill be brief.

The Captain, Eve, and Coro all
risked their lives to face the
calamity of Levarance, even
though there was nothing to be
gained from it.
Their resolve is beyond\nquestion. And mine is as well.
As for me, it's even simpler\nthan that, Mastima.
I am but thirteen years of age.\nI am still a child!
And what of it?
Children know well that the\nworld is full of things they've\nnever seen.
I shall not let my guard down.
For complacency is the\ngreatest cause of overlooking\nsomething new.
...No matter what Tika says,\nthe first name she mentions is\nalways Verda Kleiman.
Compared to a half-baked\nadult, your wit and nerve are\non an entirely different level.
I'm honored by the praise.
I can guarantee this much.
Neither the Captain, Valka, Eve,\nnor I have the option of\nstepping down from this fight.

Mastima said it herself―Givel's
actions are a threat not just to
the Twin Stars, but to the
entire universe.
Therefore, we cannot be kept\nfrom the fight simply because\nwe aren't from the Twin Stars.
For Tika, for Euwin and the\nothers, and of course for\nMastima, we shall fight!
Verda has made his point, but\nmay I double-check with the\nrest of you?
I see. ...And you?
...It is true that we, the Hardier\nWarrior of Morphus, have a\ngreat mission.

But I have learned from my
father, the greatest of all
warriors, that the core of that
mission is to protect the
peaceful lives of every living
soul.
Fighting Givel here and now is\nsomething I must do for my\nown sake as well.
Fighting Givel here and now is\nsomething I must do for my\nown sake as well.

Anyone who cannot stand by a
friend in their time of need has
no right to call themselves a
Hardier Warrior of Morphus...!
...I see.
Does that satisfy you?
My apologies. I asked a\ntactless question.

Once Tika and the others
return, I want to brief them on
the next phase of the
operation.
And also...
No, it's nothing.
I'll go check on Tika and\nRicardo. You all wait here.
I suppose living a long time\nbrings all sorts of\ncomplications.
...Verda, you really don't act\nlike a child. Are you actually\nvery old?
Who knows? Maybe it's just a\nmatter of density.
...I don't get it.
We don't have a single moment\nto lose!

If we don't defeat that Givel
quickly, the consequences
could extend beyond Daftine
and Daftes to the entire
universe!
Now! There's no time! Is\neveryone gathered!? I'm going\nto explain the plan!
Deploy the screen! Hurry,\nhurry!
Y-yes ma'am...!
I mean, Ms. Mastima, aren't you\nacting a bit high-strung? Did\nsomething good happen?
That doesn't matter, just hurry\nup!
Regardless, that's the captain's\nseat.
Coro, why are you taking\norders from Mastima instead of\nthe captain?
Eh? Ah, well, that's...
...Oh, it's nothing.
Hmm... quite so.
Eve's safety is our top priority, but since we don't know the enemy's hand, we'll have to rely on Mastima and Coro and adapt as we go.
note: glossary-waive: 臨機応変 (the idiom 'adapt as we go', not the skill Expedient Adaptation); the engine's text (gemma-4-31B-it/qat-UD-Q4_K_XL/v2+story-v1+fix/llama.cpp-b11443/t0), checked by the agent

en:
We'll gather as much intel as
possible on Baschen's Imperial
Castle and feed the data to
Coro before we set out.

Let's not sweat the small stuff.
I'm the only one who
understands the specifications
of this modified ship.
Give me the seat for now! Until\nthe briefing is over...
Why don't you just go stand in\na corner or something?
What are you all doing just\nstanding around here?
I had a feeling, but she really is\nan elusive person.

That's just Mastima's true
nature. She's a prime example
that lifespan and mental
maturity aren't exactly
proportional.

Mastima! You can't do that!
This ship belongs to the
Captain, so you have to listen
to them!
Aww, Tika... I don't want to\nlisten to some brat like this.
You're 3.7 billion years old!\nStop acting like a child!

Coro, you too! Listen to the
Captain! Mastima, you made
your own seat, so go move
over there!
And Captain, don't let Mastima\nget to you!
Now, everyone, let's get\nmoving!!
Y-yes, ma'am!
Hmph. Tika is such a stickler.
And yet, you still do as Tika\nsays.
Even I didn't realize my own\nsister had such a brisk\npersonality until I came here.
I guess when there's a big age\ngap, there are things you just\ndon't see.
...A big age gap... things you\ndon't see, huh?
Eu? What's up?
Huh? Oh, no, it's nothing.
It's... nothing.
Now, it's fine that the Captain\nis taking command, but what's\nthe outline of the operation?
Hmm. It's not that complicated.
First, we just need to destroy\nthe Holy Land Asyl and the\nblack sphere.

Asyl will surface in response to
the new crest I'm activating,
and then Coro's main cannon
will...
Boom! That's it!
Don't worry.

According to Coro, the
armament of the GFSS-3214F
is now more powerful than the
Galactic Federation's latest
cutting-edge combat ships.
Asyl will be blown to\nsmithereens in a single hit!
You make it sound so easy, but\nis it really that simple?

I told you I've been researching
the phenomena in this sector
since before the Holy War
began. Trust me on this.

For a long time now, I've been
at a stage where I could
destroy Asyl whenever I
wanted.
The reason I chose not to was\npartly because I felt it was\nhelping people.
Huh?!

Among those who emerge from
the Ladder of Moonlight, there
are occasionally individuals who
have absolutely no connection
to the Ladder and come from
far-off sectors of space.

They are swept up by
space-time rifts that have
nothing to do with the Ladder
or Asyl, and eventually wash up
here.

Once I realized that these
people were being protected, I
felt even less inclined to stop
it.
In a manner of speaking, I was\ndoing a good deed.
Well, I guess it all depends on\nhow you put it...?
However, it is a different story\nif someone other than myself\nwere to abuse it.
I absolutely cannot tolerate\nothers manipulating something I\ncreated without my permission.
That way of thinking is part of\nwhy the Ladder came into\nexistence in the first place.
Hm? Wait, Master Mastima.

If we destroy the Moonshadow
Ladder and Asyl, then
naturally, the Moonshadow
Ladder won't exist in the
future, right?
That is correct.

That's strange. If that's the
case, it doesn't explain why
Lady Tika and General Ricardo
are here.

...Mastima just said it. People
who have nothing to do with
the Ladder get washed up
here too.
I was unaware of this since I\nwas the one who protected\nTika, but...

The Daftine Space Force
escort ship commanded by
Ricardo had a vague idea of
who attacked the transport
ship.
What?!

Back in my day, the Daftine
military had intel that several
advanced planets in our
alliance were being invaded by
a mysterious force.

At the time, we'd observed an
empire ruled by a unified will
lifeform in the far reaches of
space, so I figured it was
something like that...
But as it turns out, it wasn't.\nAnd I'm the only one who\nknows.
Only you, Ricardo?
<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> Back then, I was the\nfire control officer on the\nescort ship.
That's why I saw it.

A Class 3 energy wave was
fired from a distance so
extreme I didn't think it could
possibly hit.
You'd be even more shocked if\nyou saw where it came from.

It wasn't a starship or a fixed
battery at a space station.
Those movements... no matter
how you look at it, they were
those of an organic lifeform.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> ...That's impossible...!
<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> It was a shot fired\nfrom a distance that defies all\nlogic.
Actually, I don't even know if it\nwas a "shot" at all.
But that thing captured in the\nlow Resolution footage by the\nfire-control computer...
<font color=blue>Welch</font> ...Wh-what on earth was\nthat?

<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> ...Anyway, the moment
after I saw that footage, the
escort ship I was on was hit by
an unknown impact and sunk.
I figure we probably took a\ndirect hit from Class 3 energy.
I don't know how or why I\nended up drifting toward Ex\nGiva after that, but...

<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> It wouldn't be that
far-fetched to think some
monster capable of firing Class
3 energy is involved.
<font color=blue>Henri</font> I suppose common sense\ndoesn't apply in space.

However, if we believe
Mastima's explanation, even if
the periodic Moonshadow
Ladders stop occurring,

there's still a possibility that
the current Ladder could
cause a rift in the future
space-time, right?

We can't rule out the possibility
that we were caught up in
that. We can't afford to be
complacent.

<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> Well, true enough.
Besides, it's not like anything
we do now will get Tika and me
back to our own time.
I'll just try not to overthink it.

In any case, destroying the
Ladder and Asyl now offers
more benefits than leaving
them be.
However, in the end, we must\nstop that fool Givel.

Once Asyl is destroyed, we will
likely head straight for the
Baschen Imperial Castle. From
there, it will be a
close-quarters battle.

We can't let them turn the kind
of power that can destroy Asyl
toward the Imperial Castle or
the Imperial Capital...
We can't afford to lose this\ntime.
Mastima, will you come along\nfor that fight?
I must teach that arrogant brat\na lesson.
Besides, I feel responsible for\nletting him learn about the\nGems here.
Givel learned...? Then...
What's wrong?
Hey, Eu.
Hmm? What is it, Welch?
...Take this!!
Gwah!? W-w-what was that for\nall of a sudden!!
Eu! Get your head straight!
Huh!?
What is the only thing you\nshould be thinking about right\nnow!!
Where is this coming from all\nof a sudden!
Ending the Holy War! And\nkicking Givel's ass!
I-I know that...
Then why on earth are you\nthinking about your father and\nbrother right now!!
How many years do you think\nwe've been together?! You\nthink you can fool me?!
...Haha, you got me.
Actually...
You're projecting yourself onto\nTika and Ricardo, aren't you?\nYou're so simple, Eu.
I don't want to be called simple\nby you, Welch!
Knowing how earnest and\nwell-behaved you are, Eu-bo,

You're probably thinking,
"Maybe my father and brother
had to be cold to me because
of their positions,"
Or, "Maybe I'd think the same\nway if I were in their shoes,"
Thinking all that useless crap!

You don't have to put so much
emphasis on the "useless"
part... I do have my reasons for
thinking about it...

The only thing you and Tika's
family have in common is that
the siblings have a huge age
gap!
Is there even anything to worry\nabout!?
Huh...?

...Tika and Ricardo have always
been close despite the age
gap, and they've supported
each other even through these
harsh times, right!?
Did your father or brother ever\ntry to support you or\nunderstand you?
I know. You've been trying your\nbest to find some common\nground with them, Eu.
But they have no intention of\ndoing the same.
It's obvious to anyone\nwatching. You're not like Tika\nand Ricardo.
The only person you should be\nthinking about in this situation...\nis Lady Eslyn!
...Yeah, you're right.
Make sure you don't mistake\nwho you should actually be\nworrying about.
When push comes to shove,\nyou'll want to be thinking about\nthe people who actually matter.
Not that I'm trying to deny the\nRakstar family's love, but...

In the battles ahead, don't you
think there are things you
should be worrying about more
than your father or brother?
...Yeah, you're right.
So?
Huh?
Who are you planning to think\nabout?
My comrades, I guess?
Ow! What was that for?!
Nothing! Just giving you a little\npush!
See ya! I'm heading over to\nCoro first!
...Sigh.
I mean, saying that now, after\neverything... really?
Mastima, do you have a\nmoment?
Hmm?
Do you know anything about\nthe power of the Beast Witch?

Yes, I've heard about it from
Tika and Ricardo, and I'm
aware of it through Coro and
Rekoro's records...

Unfortunately, it seems the
Beast Witch's symbol arts were
developed independently by
Givel based on the symbols I
discovered.
I haven't finished analyzing\nthem yet.
Which means I cannot remove\nthose symbols from you.
That is what you wanted to\nknow, isn't it?
It's not that I find this power\nabhorrent...

I can never forgive Givel, but
thanks to this power, the
status of the Fox-Soul people
has improved dramatically.
But...
When I think that I might have\nused this to hurt Henri's\ncomrades...
Hmm.
I'm afraid that when the time\ncomes, I might hesitate to use\nthis power.
I see.
Well, I don't see why that's a\nproblem.
What?

Whether you win or lose
against Givel, your life
continues as long as you don't
die.
This isn't some final battle for\nyour entire existence.
Even I still have moments\nwhere I worry about the nature\nand morality of my own power.

People tend to think of doubt
and worry as shackles in a
crisis, but it's also true that
they can give birth to a new
kind of strength.
If you like, I can even help you\nresearch it once the battle is\nover.
...May I take you up on that?

I don't care for the fact that
it's a crest art created by
Givel, but my curiosity
regarding new crests far
outweighs that.
...Actually.
Eh?
I wouldn't mind starting my\nresearch right now, you know?

That crest on your chest...
were you born with it? Or is it
the crest of the "Beast Witch"?
Hmm?
Hyaah!? W-wait! What are you\ndoing!?
Hmm? If I'm to study a crest, I\ncan't exactly start without\ntouching it, can I?
I-if that's the case, now is not\na good time! S-someday, when I\nfeel like it! Goodbye!
She's gone...
Hehehe. Well, I suppose that's\nhow it goes. Perhaps I teased\nher a bit too much?
It's finally time.
Yeah.
It's been a long road to get\nhere.
It has.
...If we ever run into Dad or\nMom somewhere, I bet they'd\nbe so surprised.
Yeah.
...I heard that tomorrow, Coro\nplushies are going to rain down\non Dagris.
Yeah.
Hey, big brother!
...Sorry. I was just lost in\nthought.
Yeah, I figured.
So, what were you thinking\nabout?
...How to find Dad and Mom.
Since you and I ended up like\nthis, it wouldn't be strange if\nthey were still alive.
I've been thinking about what\nto do once the battle in this\nera's Daftine is over.

It's quite different from how I
imagined things, but well, I'm
managing to get along with
you.

I thought about waiting at
Mastima's place and hoping
they'd show up, but Mastima is
the only one who can afford to
wait like that.

Besides, if they crossed
through time for the same
reason we did, there's a
chance they were sent
somewhere else entirely.
I suppose it's like trying to find\none specific grain of sand in a\ndesert...
...Yeah, you're right.

Come to think of it, Dad and
Mom were still fighting with
Grandpa and Grandma when
they left.
Even if we're living apart, we've\nstill got to find a way to get in\ntouch.
Yeah...!
But it'll probably be hard for\njust the two of us. We don't\neven have a starship.
...That's the problem... damn it.
So it feels like we're out of\noptions, right?
Dammit... this is infuriating.
...Are you worried about\nwhether you'll get along with\nMastima?
Nbyah!?
H-H-Henri!?
You look like you're wondering\nhow I knew.
H-H-H-How did you know!
Well, it's written all over your\nface.
What!! W-Where!?
No, it's not actually written\nthere.
Which is it!
...You're quite flustered.
I can tell that Master Mastima\nisn't a bad person...
But I still don't know how I\nshould act around her.
He's just so... elusive.
I see.
...I've never... heard anyone\nspeak against EnII or\nVandione...
Or say anything to deny the\nnature of Ex.
For you, Valka, it must feel as\nif your god has been denied.
Ex is not a god.
Ex is... Ex is...
Looking at your reaction, it's\nhard to think otherwise.

Well, regardless of what
happened in the past, it's true
that seeing you like this makes
me worried, Valka.
...Worried?

...Valka, you seem to rely too
heavily on your own identity as
an existence of Ex and as a
Hardier Warrior of Morphus.

Rather than taking pride in it,
aren't you driven by a
desperate fear of tarnishing
that name?
T-that's not true!
...At least, I think... I don't...
I know nothing of this "Ex" or\n"EnII."
You are the only one who does.
And from my perspective,\nValka...

From the perspective of
someone who knows nothing of
Ex, EnII, or any other Hardier
Warrior of Morphus...
You are a wonderful person.
Huh...?

You know that battle is a
terrifying thing and you never
seek it out, yet you possess
the strength and resolve to
throw yourself into the fray for
the sake of your friends.
If that isn't wonderful, I don't\nknow what is.
I-I don't! I don't think... that\nbattle is terrifying...!
...I don't... think that...
...I just thought... that I wasn't\nallowed to feel that way...

There is no such thing as a
battle that isn't terrifying. I
haven't lived as long as
Mastima, but even I know that
much.
It is simple to hold your own\nagainst Mastima.

Just face the battle head-on,
the same way you have while
spending time with the
captains.

If you do that, you will
eventually figure out how to
deal with Mastima, as someone
who shares the same universe.
...Do you really think so?
I do.
...Henri, you're kind of like my\ndad sometimes. It makes me\nfeel safe.
Henri?
...If that is how you feel...
Huh?

I'll head out first. I intended to
give you advice, but it seems I
was the one who found solace
instead.
Huh? What?
It's nothing.
Farewell.
Oh, right...
Getting over things is harder\nthan it looks...
Coro, before we set off, I'm\ngoing to run a few checks.

While I was messing with the
console earlier, I noticed some
programs and applications I've
never seen before.
I don't want some weird\noperation causing a failure\nwhen it counts.
Rest assured, Captain!
It's true that Mastima added a\nfew things while modifying me,
but she didn't touch any of my\noriginal programming!
Hmm? The ship's scanners are\nactivating on their own.
Hyah!
What!?

What is this? There's a
program set up to collect data
from normal space while we're
warping.
Doing something like that would\nmake the drive sluggish as hell.\nTake this!
Hah!
Gyah!?
Now then, Coro! Why has the\noriginal program been\ntampered with, eh?

It's defined so that under
certain conditions, Mastima's
authority overrides the
captain's!
This is getting deleted!
Awawawawa!?
I-I'm sorry...!

Individually, these aren't
harmful to us, but it's a
problem when functions the
captain doesn't know about are
running on their own.

At this rate, Mastima might
just treat the ship as her own
personal property one of these
days!
Verda, could you check me as\nwell...?
Seeing how much was done to\nCoro, I've become a little\nanxious.
Hmm, fair enough. Come over\nhere.
...Hm? What is this?
I-is something wrong!?

There's a backdoor installed.
It's set up to send the human
vital data Rekoro observed to
some unknown location.
What!?

There are a lot of entries
specifically regarding Tika.
They likely intended to keep
monitoring Tika even after she
left the satellite Mastima.
But when did this happen!?
I was threatened by Ricardo,\nbut...

I made sure Tika's personal
information was strictly
classified so it couldn't be
viewed carelessly!
...This is truly malicious. I'll have\nto demand answers from\nMastima later.
The journey of the "Coro's\nShip" must continue, even after\nwe defeat Givel.
There's no sign that the Holy\nWar will be brought to an end\nanytime soon...
The road ahead is filled with\nnothing but hardships.
That's right. We made a\npromise to Tika.

We promised Tika that we
would get her home to where
her grandfathers are... back to
Daftine.

If that is the case, then we
must become strong enough to
laugh in the face of these
hardships and blow them away!
Truly inspiring.
So inspiring, in fact, that I am\nstarting to think Verda should\nbe the captain instead.
Hmm! In that case, shall we\njust decide that the captain is\nthe pet?
No way! I won't lose! I won't\ngive in to your modifications,\nVerda! I'll fight back, Captain...!
But wait, I just realized...\nwouldn't a pet captain actually\nbe kind of cute?
Captain, shake! "Now, go fetch\nthe banana!" I could say things\nlike that...
Awa-wa-wa-wa-wa!?

Oh! The rampage suppression
device Mastima made for Coro
is working! We should definitely
keep this on him!
Ugh, I was hoping for a much\nsharper comeback...
Eve is the only one who can\nkeep you quiet with just a\ncomeback.
Indeed. We must go and\nretrieve her as soon as\npossible.

You're right! I haven't been
scolded by Eve yet, so I'm not
quite back in the swing of
things!
